decisions.summary: Past the hour, a dispatch within SAME_MESSAGE_S (5 s) of an admitted dispatch is admitted - the rest of the message the admitted one began
decisions.why: It narrows the hour guard (the GM's hourly step-back, 383): some dispatches past the hour are no longer refused. Presumed wrong. It survives on purpose and on the GM's own words. The step-back's purpose is that no new decision is taken after the hour without stepping back. The dispatches of one assistant message were all decided together, before the guard spoke, so the step-back cannot reach that decision. Refusing part of the message only splits it by hook latency (T05's five went two and three), and the refused part is re-dispatched after the step-back anyway (T05 part B item 9). The step-back still comes before every message emitted after the hour, and gates stay outside the window (D42b). The GM's amendment 5 ('I wonder if another tooling fix would make us more likely to batch commands') asks for more batching, and a guard that splits a batch penalizes exactly that. PREMISE this ruling rests on: the plan carries out 'same message' as nearness in time (5 s from an admitted dispatch), not as the message's identity. The ruling covers only the plan's stated bound, 'the rest of the message it began'. A window that admits a dispatch from a FOLLOWING message, for example one emitted within 5 s of a dispatch that returned at once, or a chain that carries past the message, would be outside this ruling and would need a new one. The test should hold that bound. Approach item 3's 'the batching hook's same-turn window, widened' is read as a wider value used by checkpoint.due only. D42 names only checkpoint.due and stepback_bundle.refusals. A change to the batching hook's own window would reach beyond the arbiter's fix.
